answer.reason: An injected failure at the first xmlXIncludeNewRef allocation sets the harness failure flag. The changed memory reporter does not set the XInclude context’s errNo, so the existing check expects false and aborts. The removed reporter did set errNo for this same failure.
answer.finite_witness: Frame a main entity with URL main.xml and document <r xmlns:xi="http://www.w3.org/2003/XInclude"><xi:include href="other.xml"/></r>. Set the four-byte allocation selector to the finite index of xmlXIncludeNewRef’s first xmlMalloc after the harness enables injection. Add an unused framed entity with enough bytes that size + 100 exceeds that index.

scope_contract.reason: The old entry invokes xmlXIncludeProcessNode and checks its XInclude context error after processing; reference creation and its memory error reporting are inside that operation.

feasible_trigger.reason: The framed input can provide a valid include and select its reference allocation as the injected failure. Padding an unused entity can make the input-size modulus admit that finite allocation index.

observable_consequence.reason: The replacement reporter writes the global error but leaves the zero-initialized XInclude context error unchanged. The getter therefore supplies a false expectation while the allocation-failure flag is true, and the existing check aborts.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: A valid document gives a nonnull context. Failure at the first reference allocation returns before resource loading or fallback can report another error; the complete old entry has no other XInclude error check before this assertion.

identity_preserved.reason: Both sides assess the same failure at xmlXIncludeNewRef’s first allocation and the same old-harness error check. The removed reporter set ctxt->errNo; the added reporter does not. The g0007 change concerns another reference allocation failure and does not replace this tuple.
